finding_1_handler_fault_stack.was: EntryError had no stack field, and both handler-fault recording paths in perform.ts built the entry error from code, kind and message only, so the stack of whatever the handler threw was discarded.

located.packages/lang/src/journal.ts:24-29: interface EntryError { code, kind, message, detail? } - no stack
located.packages/lang/src/perform.ts:340-343: effect site: const error: EntryError = recorded !== undefined ? recorded.error : { code: carried ?? "L4000", kind: "handler-fault", message: messageOf(e) }
located.packages/lang/src/perform.ts:500-501: waitUntil probe site: the same expression, which a fix at the effect site alone would have left open

change.packages/lang/src/journal.ts: EntryError gains an optional readonly stack?: string, documented as written only when the thrown value carried one.
change.packages/lang/src/errors.ts: new exported stackOf(v: unknown): string | undefined, the guard: reads .stack off a possibly-null value and keeps it only when it is a non-empty string.
change.packages/lang/src/perform.ts: both handler-fault sites spread the recorded error and add stack only when stackOf returned one. The EffectError branch (recordableError) and the plain-throw branch both get it.
change.spec/cotal-lang.md: the journal entry shape now names error.stack, since the spec documents that record.

guards: absent stack (a primitive throw) records no stack rather than the string "undefined"
a non-string stack (e.g. the number 42) records no stack
an empty-string stack is treated as absent

proof.test: packages/lang/smoke/journal.smoke.ts, the cell '// ---- and a handler fault carries WHERE it was thrown from'
proof.how: drives the real interpreter with a handler whose turn throws, then reads error.stack back OFF THE RECORDED JOURNAL ENTRY, not off the raised error. Asserting on the raised error would pass with the field dropped.
assertions: a handler fault records the STACK of the error that was thrown, read back off the recorded entry
...and it is the stack, not the message repeated into the field
the recorded stack survives a serialized round trip, which is the form a later reader gets
a primitive throw records NO stack rather than inventing one, and still records the fault
a thrown value whose `stack` is not a string records no stack, and the rest of the fault is unharmed

finding_2_void_revert_gate.was: implementations/runtime/smoke/host-starvation.smoke.ts imported POLL_ATTEMPTS by name from ../src/host-starvation.js. That export is one the fix ADDED, so against base the file failed at module instantiation: exit 1 with zero assertions executed. The non-zero exit was a broken import, not a detection, which is why the gate was VOID.

change.import: the named import of POLL_ATTEMPTS was dropped; the module is also pulled in as a namespace (import * as starvation) and POLL_ATTEMPTS is read off it defensively, falling back to STARVED_ATTEMPTS when the export is absent. A namespace import always links, so the file instantiates on both trees.
change.assertion: cell 1e's 'after a bounded number of reads' no longer asserts equality with the constant. It now asserts the BEHAVIOUR: attempts > 1 (it re-read at all, which a tree that treats a late reply as a fault fails, since that raises on the first attempt) and attempts <= POLL_ATTEMPTS (it ended). The ceiling is a sanity bound; the discriminating claim is the re-read.
change.cell_1f: left reading the fallback-backed ceiling, where the bound was already documented in-file as a sanity bound rather than the discriminating claim.
